column4: Neolithic stone-circle walls (Arbor Low, UK)
column6: Preferentially associated with wall microbiome (indicator OTU, 0.98% wall vs 0.02% sediment)

Blastocatellaceae/Blastocatella confirmed as a top family, >50% of sequences in 10 samples.

column4: Austrian historical chapels/castle (Johannes Chapel, Rappottenstein, St. Rupert Chapel)

column4: Johannes Chapel, Castle Rappottenstein, Saint Rupert Chapel; Convent of Christ; Coimbra Cathedral

Convent of Christ: Rosado et al., "Assessment of microbiota present on a Portuguese historical stone convent using high-throughput sequencing approaches," MicrobiologyOpen 2020, 9:e1030. doi:10.1002/mbo3.1030 (PMC7294311). Coimbra: Miller et al./Rosado group, "Bacterial and Archaeal Structural Diversity in Several Biodeterioration Patterns on the Limestone Walls of the Old Cathedral of Coimbra" (PMC8065406) — Rubrobacter reported as "the most prominent bacterial genus when considering all sites." | Also corroborated at a 5th independent site, Chaalis Abbey, France: Mihajlovski et al. 2017, Int. Biodeter. Biodegrad. 120:161-169 — Rubrobacter-related phylotypes dominated (60.4% of clones) the Discolored Area library there, consistent with the genus's established rosy/grey discoloration role.
column12: PARTICULARLY IMPORTANT: Rubrobacter recurs as a dominant pigmented biodeteriogen across at least 4 independent studies/countries (Austria, Portugal x2, and cross-referenced at Longmen China too) — one of the best cross-validated genera in the whole table. Now cross-validated at a 5th independent site (Chaalis Abbey, France) — among the most robustly confirmed genera in the whole table.
